main_text.l: Theologiæ Caluinistarum libros tres, in
quibus ceu in tabella quadam, quasi ad ocu-
lum plusquam ducentos viginti tres errores
Sacramentariorum publicis scriptis, verbis
proprijs, & auctorum nominibus indicatis,
demonstratur, eos de nullo fere doctrinæ
Christianæ articulo recte sentire, addita si-
mul veræ sententiæ assertione, & contrariæ
opinionis refutatione. Francofurti 1592.
in 4. Dies me deficeret, & charta, si vel-
lem omnia, quæ Martinus Lutherus, Phi-
lippus Melanchthon, Franciscus Stancka-
rus, alijq; scripserunt, ediderunt[?]que contra
Caluinistas, & contra Lutheranos Cal-
uinistæ, in medium proferre. Præ manibus
omnium sunt certa dogmata, in quibus Lu-
therani a Caluinistis, seu Sacramentarijs dis-
sentiunt, & Sacramentarij a Lutheranis in-
grauissimis fidei dogmatibus. Vin plura ?
Non eadem dicunt, tenentque inter se Trinitarij. Sacramentarij Sacramentarios
mutuis scriptis damnant, Anabaptistæ Anabaptistas, Lutherani Lutheranos. Et quod
manifeste perridiculum est, Caluinus,
Melanchthon, Luthe rus a se ipsis in potissimis
discordant: nec quid inter ipsos certum fit,
nec ipsi sciunt, nec alij capiunt. Ita tene-
brarum potestas inter eos conualuit, ue-
aiant, negent eodem ipso momento, & dum

page.notes: Page number reads "391"; the last digit is printed in a form close to "r" ("39r"), read here as 1. The left and right scan edges show partial red-brown letters ("pi", "di", "al" and similar) belonging to the neighbouring page or to a stain; they are not transcribed. The hyphenated line end "ve-" / "aiant" is doubtful: the word may read "ue-", "vt" or other, and is given as "ue-aiant". "ediderunt[?]que" is uncertain. The paragraph is taken as continuing from the previous page, since the first line runs on mid-sentence.
